standard_prerequisites.name: Finite-state Poisson equation and geometric ergodicity
standard_prerequisites.statement: For an irreducible aperiodic finite chain, V - PV = g is solvable for the centered reward g; the conditional covariance satisfies ||E(Sigma_k) - Sigma_infinity||_op <= C rho^(k-1) for some rho in (0,1).
standard_prerequisites.use: Produces the potential V, the martingale differences m_k and the geometric tails behind the two-sided covariance sandwich. No rate is assumed.

standard_prerequisites.name: Vector martingale Wasserstein comparison
standard_prerequisites.reference: source 199-281 with its complete proof at 283-747, both kept as supporting obligations
standard_prerequisites.statement: d_W(W_n, n^(-1/2)V_1^(1/2)Z) is bounded by two Taylor remainders multiplied by Tr(D_k) plus the signed covariance-interaction term Delta_n.
standard_prerequisites.use: Applied to the martingale part after the boundary term is removed. Its signed interaction is exactly what forces the k-dependent centring in the nonstationary proof.

standard_prerequisites.name: Hessian-weight variation and Gaussian smoothing bounds
standard_prerequisites.statement: With H_k = V_k^(-1/2) A_{k,h}(F_(k-1)) V_k^(-1/2), the Mehler representation plus ||grad^j P_A h|| <= C||A^(-1/2)||^(j-1) for j = 2,3,4 gives sup_h sum_k E||H_k - H_(k-1)||_op <= C(1-beta)^(-2) n^((1-beta)/2).
standard_prerequisites.use: Supplies the three spatial/internal/external comparison estimates that the nonstationary proof re-derives from the covariance increments instead of stationarity.

standard_prerequisites.name: Matrix square root Lipschitz continuity and Gaussian coupling
standard_prerequisites.statement: On the positive-definite cone the square-root map is locally Lipschitz, so coupling n^(-1/2)V_1^(1/2)Z and Sigma_infinity^(1/2)Z through one standard normal vector costs O(n^(-1)).
standard_prerequisites.use: Converts 1/n V_1 = Sigma_infinity + O(n^(-1)) into a Wasserstein comparison of the limiting Gaussian.

core_obligations: Split U_n into the martingale part W_n and the boundary term (V(X_0) - V(X_n))/sqrt(n), which stays valid for an arbitrary initial distribution, and retain its O(n^(-1/2)) contribution (source 1141-1153).

Rebuild the nonstationary covariance sandwich c(n-k+1)I <= V_k <= C(n-k+1)I from ||E(Sigma_k) - Sigma_infinity||_op <= C rho^(k-1), and read off Tr(D_k) <= C/(n-k+1) so that the two Taylor remainders of the supporting theorem stay at C(1-beta)^(-2)n^(-beta/2) (1161-1230).

Centre the covariance Poisson solution: solve Phi - PPhi = Sigma_infinity - v and decompose E(Sigma_k) - Sigma_k = Phi_(k-1)~ - Phi_k~ + Gamma_k, noting that E[Phi(X_k)] is now k-dependent (1232-1287).

Re-derive the Hessian-weight variation bound without stationarity, using V_(k-1) - V_k = E(Sigma_(k-1)) and V_k - V_(k+1) = E(Sigma_k), to get sup_h sum_k E||H_k - H_(k-1)||_op <= C(1-beta)^(-2)n^((1-beta)/2) (1333-1351).
Optimise beta = 1 - 2/log n to pass from the beta-uniform bound to O((log n)^2/sqrt(n)), absorbing the finitely many remaining n into C (1359-1376).

proof_roadmap.step: Split U_n into W_n plus the boundary term (V(X_0) - V(X_n))/sqrt(n); geometric ergodicity gives ||E(Sigma_k) - Sigma_infinity||_op <= C rho^(k-1), hence 1/n V_1 = Sigma_infinity + O(n^(-1)), compared with the limiting Gaussian through one standard normal vector.
Sandwich V_k from the geometric tails, pass to Tr(D_k) <= C/(n-k+1), and bound the two martingale Taylor remainders by C(1-beta)^(-2)n^(-beta/2).

Solve Phi - PPhi = Sigma_infinity - v, decompose the covariance error with the k-dependent centring E[Phi(X_k)], and re-derive the Hessian-weight variation bound from the nonstationary covariance increments.
Apply the supporting martingale theorem to W_n, compare the Gaussian targets, and choose beta = 1 - 2/log n to reach O((log n)^2/sqrt(n)).

difficulty_reason: The claim removes both stationarity and periodicity from the finite-state Markov-chain CLT and allows an arbitrary initial law, so the stationary asymptotic covariance cannot be reused as it stands. With V_k = sum_{j=k}^n E(Sigma_j) and D_k = V_k^(-1/2)E(Sigma_k)V_k^(-1/2), the proof must rebuild the two-sided sandwich c(n-k+1)I <= V_k <= C(n-k+1)I from geometric ergodicity alone (source 1186-1204), read off Tr(D_k) <= C/(n-k+1) (1217-1224) and thereby keep the two Taylor remainders of the retained martingale theorem at C(1-beta)^(-2)n^(-beta/2) (1225-1230). The non-routine step is the covariance-interaction term at 1232-1357: the bounded solution Phi of Phi - PPhi = Sigma_infinity - v must be centred by E[Phi(X_k)], which is now k-dependent, giving E(Sigma_k) - Sigma_k = Phi_(k-1)~ - Phi_k~ + Gamma_k (1276-1287), and summation by parts then needs ||H_k - H_(k-1)||, which is re-derived from the covariance increments V_(k-1) - V_k = E(Sigma_(k-1)) and V_k - V_(k+1) = E(Sigma_k) rather than from stationarity (1333-1351). This is not a formal substitution into the stationary theorem, and the paper's own general state-space extension later reuses exactly this nonstationary argument (1441-1443).

compared.difference: That item is the abstract martingale theorem and carries no Markov chain, no initial-law discussion and no Poisson equation. compared.actual_statement: source 946-962: stationary finite-state irreducible (possibly periodic) chain CLT, proof 964-1120
compared.difference: That card keeps the chain stationary, so E(Sigma_k) = Sigma_infinity and V_k = (n-k+1)Sigma_infinity is available for free. The new claim removes stationarity, allows an arbitrary initial distribution and aperiodicity, and therefore needs the covariance sandwich 1186-1224, the k-dependent Poisson centring 1232-1287 and the nonstationary variation bound 1333-1351; its proof spans 1140-1377 are disjoint from that card's 964-1120, and the stationary theorem appears here only as context.
Different source and different mechanism: a Wasserstein-p CLT rate built from local dependence, not a finite-state Markov-chain Poisson-equation argument. No shared span or hypothesis.
That item concerns solvability of Poisson's equation for Wasserstein-contractive chains; it bounds no distance to a Gaussian limit and contains no martingale or Stein step.

editorial_notes: The fixed source is arXiv 2401.15719v5; its footnote on page 1 states that this version corrects errors of the Math of OR published version, and the official v5 archive names its main file arxiv-v6.tex, which is an internal filename and not a different arXiv version.

Only the nonstationary aperiodic corollary 1125-1138 is counted here. The stationary theorem 946-962 is carried as context for the notation it fixes ('retain the notation from the stationary theorem') and no count is assigned to it in this card.

The abstract martingale theorem 199-281 and its complete proof 283-747, and the Hessian-weight variation lemma 818-942, are carried as supporting obligations because the proof applies them at 1226, 1333 and 1359; neither receives a separate count.

The letter h denotes both the Lipschitz test function and, in the Poisson-equation display at 785-788, the potential is named V; the extracted spans keep the source's own naming and no symbol has been renamed or repaired.
